review.tagline: Go engine that ingests content streams for hybrid search and keyword alerts
review.summary: Quivr V2 is a Go service that durably ingests text and documents, indexes them in Weaviate for lexical, semantic and hybrid search, and runs saved queries as subscriptions that produce matches and signed webhooks. State lives in PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage, with Temporal for orchestration and plugins for connectors and alert rules. The README marks it as evaluation stage with a v0 API that may change.
review.audience: Engineers building search and alerts over content feeds
strengths: Idempotent writes and immutable Versions; search index can be rebuilt from PostgreSQL and S3
Hybrid search rehydrates and re-authorizes every hit; outages return errors, not empty results
Subscriptions with keyword, meaning and described alerts, plus signed webhook delivery
Prometheus metrics, optional OpenTelemetry tracing, and documented worker autoscaling and upgrades
weaknesses: README says evaluation stage, API v0 may change, not for production
Heavy stack: PostgreSQL, Temporal, Weaviate, S3 storage and a TEI embedding server
No chat or LLM answer generation described; differs from the earlier Quivr assistant
Described alerts send article text to TypeSafe; last release is February 2025
needs: Needs PostgreSQL 17, Temporal, Weaviate, S3-compatible storage (SeaweedFS locally), TEI (multilingual-e5-small), Docker Compose
Models: multilingual-e5-small (384-dim, local TEI), custom embedding model server, hosted embedding API
